data.name: Hazir
data.gender_notes: Hazir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'h-z-r' which means 'to be present, to be ready'. In Islamic tradition, it represents the state of being prepared for Allah's will. The name Hazir carries the meaning “Present, Ready” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hazir usually hope their child will grow to embody present, ready and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifies the presence of God in every moment
data.etymology: Hazir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Present, Ready.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hazir total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: حاضر
in_arabic.meaning: حاضر يعني حاضر و موجود و قابل للاستدعاء
in_arabic.long_meaning: حاضر هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الشخص الذي يكون دائمًا حاضرًا وموجودًا وقابلًا للاستدعاء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع بمعنى حاضر و شاهد. و يعتبر اسم حاضر من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني جميلة و عميقة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: حاضر
in_urdu.meaning: حاضر مطلب حاضر ہونا، موجود ہونا، قابلِ طلب ہونا
in_urdu.long_meaning: حاضر ایک عربی मूल کا مذکر نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے حاضر ہونا، موجود ہونا، یا قابلِ طلب ہونا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے اور اکثر اس کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں شاهد یا حاضر کے معنی میں کیا گیا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے لیے یہ نام خاص معانی رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हाज़िर
in_hindi.meaning: हाज़िर मतलब मौजूद होना, उपस्थित होना, बुलाने योग्य होना
in_hindi.long_meaning: हाज़िर एक अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम है जिसका अर्थ है मौजूद होना, उपस्थित होना या बुलाने योग्य होना। यह नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण है और अक्सर इसका उल्लेख कुरआन में उपस्थित या شاهد के अर्थ में किया गया है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का विशेष महत्व है।

in_pashto.name: حاضر
in_pashto.meaning: حاضر معنی موجود وی، حاضر وی، د بللو وړ وی
in_pashto.long_meaning: حاضر د یو مذکر نوم دی چی عربي اصله لري او معنی یې دی موجود وی، حاضر وی، یا د بللو وړ وی. دا نوم د افغانستان په اسلامی کیلنڈر کی اهميت لري او ډیری وختونه په قرآن کریم کی د شاهد یا حاضر په معنی کی اخیستل شوی دی. په پښتنو او افغانانو کی دا نوم خاص معنی لري.

in_english.name: Hazir
in_english.meaning: Hazir means being present, existing, or being ready to be called
in_english.long_meaning: Hazir is a masculine name of Arabic origin, meaning being present, existing, or ready to be called. It is mentioned in the Quran in several contexts as 'present' or 'witness'. The name holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing readiness and presence. It is used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting a connection to Arabic linguistic heritage.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Hazir in Arabic means "present" or "ready". It symbolizes being prepared and present for Allah at all times, and having a heart that is always receptive to His call.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah - Volume 13, Page 113 The name Hazir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the caliphate of Ali ibn Abi Talib, a man named Hazrat ibn Ziyad al-Kindi was appointed as the governor of Iraq. He was a just and capable ruler, and during his tenure, he was able to bring peace and stability to the region.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Masudi's Muruj Al-Dhahab - Volume 2, Page 417 The name Hazir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the Buwayhid dynasty, there was a famous poet named Hazrat ibn Hakim al-Qudsi. He was a master of Arabic poetry and was known for his beautiful verses. He lived during the time of the Buwayhid ruler Adud al-Dawla.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Hazir' in the Islamic context refers to being present and fully engaged in the moment. This concept is increasingly popular in modern Islamic spirituality as a means of self-improvement and mindfulness. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to sharing inspiring quotes, art, and practices that promote being present. On YouTube, there are videos on mindfulness meditation, mindful eating, and other aspects of living in the moment. Lastly, podcasts, such as 'The Mindful Muslim' and 'Islam and Mindfulness', offer guided practices, discussions, and interviews on the topic of being present and applying it to daily life.
